note: The route through the case. A finding is a titled stretch of years with one lead card; every entry is filed under the last finding whose `from` year is not after it. Assignment is arithmetic, so nothing is orphaned and a new entry files itself. Add a finding by adding a row here — never by tagging entries.

findings.title: Before the machines
findings.blurb: The mathematics of thinking gets written down decades before anything exists that could run it.

findings.title: The brain as a circuit
findings.blurb: A nerve cell is modelled as a logic gate, information is given a unit, and the question stops being whether machines can think and becomes how you would tell.

findings.title: The field is named
findings.blurb: A summer workshop gives the work a name and a goal, and the money follows the promise.

findings.title: The first doubts
findings.blurb: A pattern-matching script convinces people it understands them, and a government report asks what any of it has actually delivered.

findings.title: The book that closed the door
findings.blurb: One mathematical result about what a single-layer network cannot do is read as a verdict on the whole approach.

findings.title: The first winter
findings.blurb: Funding stops. The work that continues is narrow, useful and careful not to call itself artificial intelligence.

findings.title: Rules for hire, then the second winter
findings.blurb: Hand-written rules are sold as products, the market discovers what they cost to maintain, and the funding goes away again.

findings.title: Statistics quietly wins
findings.blurb: While the field is out of fashion, learning from data beats writing down rules — in translation, in handwriting, at backgammon, and eventually in public. The unglamorous years are when the conditions assemble.

findings.title: Data, silicon and a benchmark
findings.blurb: Graphics hardware becomes programmable, someone labels fourteen million images, and the three missing pieces are finally in the same room.

findings.title: The field is bought
findings.blurb: One result on one benchmark starts a bidding war. After this the story stops being about ideas and becomes about who owns them.

findings.title: The counterweight
findings.blurb: A lab is founded to stop one company owning the outcome, and a program wins a game everyone said was a decade away.

findings.title: Attention, and the first harms
findings.blurb: Eight pages make scale the only lever that matters — and in the same stretch the failures stop being hypothetical.

findings.title: Scale becomes a business
findings.blurb: The nonprofit takes the investment, the models get an order of magnitude larger, and the people who write down the risks start leaving.

findings.title: Contact with the public
findings.blurb: Capability meets a hundred million people in two months, and every lab's release calendar is rewritten by competition rather than readiness.

findings.title: The scramble
findings.blurb: Governments convene, courts meet their first fabricated citations, and a five-day boardroom fight settles who actually controls a frontier lab.

findings.title: Rules, money and the first breaches
findings.blurb: The first comprehensive law is adopted, the buildout reaches industrial scale, and the shared infrastructure everyone depends on is attacked.

findings.title: Reasoning gets cheap
findings.blurb: Thinking longer at answer time becomes a technique rather than a secret, and the price of the frontier collapses in a single session.

findings.title: Agents, and the supply chain
findings.blurb: Models start holding jobs rather than answering questions, and the repository everyone trains from becomes the way in.

findings.title: Still open
findings.blurb: Everything past here is a scenario, not a forecast. Read the confidence, not the date — and check whether anything on the board argues for it at all.
